concept.title: Improved Bound for Signless Laplacian Spectral Radius of $tK_3$-Free Graphs
concept.concept_description: The paper proves that for $t \geq 2$ and $n \geq 28t-17$, the unique $tK_3$-free graph of order $n$ maximizing the signless Laplacian spectral radius is $K_{t-1} \vee K_{\lfloor (n-t+1)/2 \rfloor, \lceil (n-t+1)/2 \rceil}$. For $t=2$, this holds for all $n \geq 6 = 3 \cdot 2$. We conjecture that the bound $28t-17$ can be universally improved to $3t$ for all $t \geq 2$.
concept.mathematical_framing: The paper proves that for $t \geq 2$ and $n \geq 28t-17$, the unique $tK_3$-free graph of order $n$ maximizing the signless Laplacian spectral radius is $K_{t-1} \vee K_{\lfloor (n-t+1)/2 \rfloor, \lceil (n-t+1)/2 \rceil}$. For $t=2$, this holds for all $n \geq 6 = 3 \cdot 2$. We conjecture that the bound $28t-17$ can be universally improved to $3t$ for all $t \geq 2$.
concept.lean_guess: Extend the stability method used in the paper by analyzing the structure of near-extremal graphs for smaller $n$. Leverage the known exact result for $t=2$ ($n \geq 6$) as a base case. Use spectral perturbation arguments to show that any deviation from the conjectured extremal graph reduces the spectral radius when $n \geq 3t$. The key is to tighten the eigenvalue interlacing bounds and degree sequence estimates that currently require $n \geq 28t-17$.

concept.title: Combinatorial Nerve Chain Homotopy Equivalence
concept.concept_description: Let $X$ be a finite simplicial complex covered by subcomplexes $A_1, \dots, A_k$. For each non-empty subset $S \subseteq [k]$, let $Y_S = \cap_{i \in S} A_i$, and let $V_S$ be an acyclic gradient vector field on $Y_S$. The combinatorial nerve chain complex $C_*(X; V)$ is defined such that for each integer $n$, the chain group $C_n(X; V)$ is the direct sum over all non-empty subsets $S \subseteq [k]$ of the free abelian group generated by the $(n - |S| + 1)$-dimensional critical simplices of $V_S$ on $Y_S$. Equipped with the differentials combining the internal Morse differentials and the nerve face maps defined via gradient trajectories between the intersections, $C_*(X; V)$ is chain homotopy equivalent to the simplicial chain complex of $X$.
concept.mathematical_framing: Let $X$ be a finite simplicial complex covered by subcomplexes $A_1, \dots, A_k$. For each non-empty subset $S \subseteq [k]$, let $Y_S = \cap_{i \in S} A_i$, and let $V_S$ be an acyclic gradient vector field on $Y_S$. The combinatorial nerve chain complex $C_*(X; V)$ is defined such that for each integer $n$, the chain group $C_n(X; V)$ is the direct sum over all non-empty subsets $S \subseteq [k]$ of the free abelian group generated by the $(n - |S| + 1)$-dimensional critical simplices of $V_S$ on $Y_S$. Equipped with the differentials combining the internal Morse differentials and the nerve face maps defined via gradient trajectories between the intersections, $C_*(X; V)$ is chain homotopy equivalent to the simplicial chain complex of $X$.
concept.lean_guess: Construct the combinatorial nerve chain complex as the total complex of a double complex formed by the Morse complexes of the intersections and the face maps of the nerve (defined via gradient trajectories), then establish a chain homotopy equivalence to the simplicial chain complex of X by verifying that the spectral sequence associated to this double complex converges to the homology of X and is isomorphic to the Leray spectral sequence of the cover.

concept.mathematical_framing: We conjecture that for every projective plane of order q (q ≥ 2), the family of its lines (a 2-(q^2+q+1, q+1, 1) design) defines a fair ℓ‑regular mechanism whose expected coupon‑collection time strictly exceeds that of the fully random model on the same parameters, and that this mechanism attains the maximal possible expected time among all uniform ℓ‑regular families on the underlying n‑set.
concept.lean_guess: Formalize the expected collection time as a function of a family ℱ using the standard Markov chain model. Compute the exact expected time for the uniform random model (n H_n). For the projective plane family, use the known intersection numbers (any two distinct lines intersect in exactly one point) to derive the transition matrix, which can be expressed in terms of the design parameters. Show that the spectral gap is smaller than that of the random model, implying a larger mean hitting time. Verify the inequality for small q by explicit computation, and outline an inductive argument for the general q based on the eigenvalues of the associated association scheme.
